scope: >=1-minute strategies; papers and online material are design priors, never LuminaQuant performance evidence
principles: Reuse existing strategy classes before adding another signal class.
Translate paper horizons into wall-clock time, not raw bar counts.
Rank and gate on purged validation; locked OOS is report-only and opened once.
Count every horizon, filter, overlay, allocator, cost scenario, and failed run in the trial ledger.
A single-leg funding or basis signal is directional derivatives alpha, not delta-neutral carry.
Missing metrics, CSCV/PBO, SPA, costs, capacity, or timestamp alignment fail closed; NA is never zero.

sources.title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
sources.authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski
sources.supports: Crypto market returns exhibit short weekly time-series momentum in the paper sample; the implementable design signs prior three-week own returns and holds one week.
sources.limitations: Sample ends in 2018; paper returns do not establish current, costed, short-feasible LuminaQuant performance.

sources.title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
sources.authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski; Xi Wu
sources.supports: Market, size, and short-horizon cross-sectional momentum explain much of the paper-sample crypto cross-section; one-to-four-week return sorts are the relevant observational and predictive benchmark.
sources.limitations: The working design does not prove feasible borrow, point-in-time universe construction, or current net profitability.

sources.title: Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Momentum in the Cryptocurrency Market under Realistic Assumptions
sources.authors: Chulwoo Han; Byeongguk Kang; Jehyeon Ryu
sources.publication: Auckland Centre for Financial Research working paper / SSRN 4675565
sources.supports: A realistic-fee, liquidation-aware design prior for short-horizon time-series momentum and separate long/short attribution.
sources.limitations: Not peer reviewed; reported robustness cannot be transferred to repository strategies or venues.

sources.title: A Trend Factor for the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
sources.authors: Christian Fieberg; Gerrit Liedtke; Thorsten Poddig; Thomas Walker; Adam Zaremba
sources.publication: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 60(7)
sources.supports: Composite price, volume, and volatility forecasts can be tested as a preregistered cross-sectional trend factor.
sources.limitations: A trained 28-indicator elastic-net composite is not evidence for plain return momentum or arbitrary repository filters.

sources.title: Psychological Anchoring Effect and Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
sources.authors: Yuecheng Jia; Betty Simkins; Shu Yan; Hongyu Zhang; Jiangyu Zhao
sources.supports: Weekly cross-sectional nearness-to-52-week-high is a testable crypto anchoring signal.
sources.limitations: Published paper-sample spreads do not validate 30-week fallbacks, young-coin shortcuts, inverse-vol sizing, or repository net returns.

sources.title: Time Series Momentum
sources.authors: Tobias Moskowitz; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
sources.supports: Own-return sign and ex-ante inverse-volatility sizing are canonical diversified-futures trend design priors.
sources.limitations: Non-crypto futures evidence; it does not support arbitrary KER, ADX, multi-horizon agreement, or repository holding gates.

sources.title: Momentum Has Its Moments
sources.authors: Pedro Barroso; Pedro Santa-Clara
sources.supports: Lagged realized volatility of the momentum portfolio itself can be tested as a separately counted risk-scaling variant.
sources.limitations: Equity-factor evidence; it does not validate BTC benchmark-vol scaling or an always-on wrapper.

sources.title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
sources.authors: Alan Moreira; Tyler Muir
sources.supports: Inverse lagged variance is a testable factor-risk scaling prior.
sources.limitations: Not crypto-specific; the rule uses the same factor's variance and may lever, unlike the current repository overlay.

sources.title: Momentum Crashes
sources.authors: Kent Daniel; Tobias Moskowitz
sources.supports: Momentum risk is state-dependent and crash-risk scaling merits a preregistered challenger.
sources.limitations: The published continuous conditional mean/variance rule is not a hard repository drawdown/volatility-z gate.

sources.title: On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
sources.authors: Scott Cederburg; Michael O'Doherty; Feifei Wang; Xuemin Yan
sources.supports: Volatility management must compete against unscaled controls rather than be assumed beneficial.
sources.limitations: Equity-strategy counterevidence, not crypto calibration.

sources.title: Trading Volume and Liquidity Provision in Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.authors: Daniele Bianchi; Mykola Babiak; Alexander Dickerson
sources.supports: Short-term crypto reversal is linked to liquidity provision and is strongest in less active, smaller, volatile, illiquid pairs.
sources.limitations: Gross reversal/liquidity premia can be compensation for spread, adverse selection, inventory, and capacity risk; OHLCV bars cannot prove executable profit.

sources.title: Up or Down? Short-Term Reversal, Momentum, and Liquidity Effects in Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.authors: Adam Zaremba; Mehmet Huseyin Bilgin; Huaigang Long; Aleksander Mercik; Jan J. Szczygielski
sources.supports: Reversal versus continuation is horizon- and liquidity-dependent and should be tested with separate legs and costs.
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional paper results do not validate a specific z-score, VWAP, shock, or intraday implementation.

sources.title: Pairs Trading in Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.authors: Milan Fil; Ladislav Kristoufek
sources.supports: Crypto pair mean reversion can be evaluated at five-minute, hourly, and daily horizons with explicit transaction-cost sensitivity.
sources.limitations: Historical pair results do not prove stationarity, borrow, synchronized fills, or current venue profitability.

sources.title: Order Flow Analysis of Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.authors: Eduard Silantyev
sources.supports: Trade-flow/order-flow imbalance explains contemporaneous high-frequency crypto price changes and is a valid microstructure feature hypothesis.
sources.limitations: Contemporaneous explanatory power is not next-bar alpha; executable use needs point-in-time order-book/trade data and latency costs.

sources.title: Market Impact and Efficiency in Cryptoassets Markets
sources.authors: Emilio Barucci; Santiago Giuffra Moncayo; Daniele Marazzina
sources.supports: Lagged order flow and market impact should be studied by horizon with an explicit efficiency/execution test.
sources.limitations: A lagged association does not establish capacity- and latency-adjusted live returns.

sources.title: A Seesaw Effect in the Cryptocurrency Market: Understanding the Return Cross Predictability of Cryptocurrencies
sources.authors: Yuecheng Jia; Yangru Wu; Shu Yan; Yuzheng Liu
sources.supports: Negative intraday cross-predictability is an external benchmark for cross-asset lead-lag experiments.
sources.limitations: The paper's data, LASSO, timing, and cost setup are not equivalent to repository bar-level lead-lag classes.

sources.title: How Investible Is Bitcoin? Analyzing the Liquidity and Transaction Costs of Bitcoin Markets
sources.authors: Anne H. Dyhrberg; Sean Foley; Jiri Svec
sources.supports: High-frequency crypto research must measure quoted/effective spreads and intraday liquidity rather than assume close-price execution.
sources.limitations: Older three-exchange Bitcoin evidence does not set current symbol-specific cost parameters.

sources.title: Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy
sources.authors: Tomoki Kurihara; Takuji Matsumoto
sources.supports: Binance one-minute evidence supports BTC t-1 price transmission primarily toward lower-liquidity, low-trade-count altcoins.
sources.limitations: The paper's 2 bp fee and short OOS windows omit observed spread, impact, and capacity; it does not validate a fixed four-leader set.

sources.title: On the Intraday Behavior of Bitcoin
sources.authors: Giacomo De Nicola
sources.supports: Negative first-order autocorrelation is visible from one-minute data, with economically more interpretable reversal at one-to-four-hour horizons.
sources.limitations: The paper attributes much of 1-15 minute reversal to bid-ask bounce and warns that fees plus spread likely erase the few-bps gross result.

sources.title: Intraday Return Predictability in the Cryptocurrency Markets: Momentum, Reversal, or Both
sources.authors: Zhuzhu Wen; Elie Bouri; Yahua Xu; Yang Zhao
sources.publication: North American Journal of Economics and Finance
sources.supports: Five-minute inputs show state-dependent hourly momentum and reversal around jumps, liquidity, announcements, and regimes.
sources.limitations: It does not establish a universal VWAP or z-score rule and does not transfer its execution economics to LuminaQuant.

sources.title: Bitcoin Wild Moves: Evidence from Order Flow Toxicity and Price Jumps
sources.authors: Atiwat Kitvanitphasu; Khine Kyaw; Tanakorn Likitapiwat; Sirimon Treepongkaruna
sources.publication: Research in International Business and Finance
sources.supports: Transaction-derived one-minute VPIN is persistent and predicts future Bitcoin jump occurrence as a risk variable.
sources.limitations: VPIN is unsigned and does not validate directional trend confirmation or net trading profit.

sources.title: Assessing Measures of Order Flow Toxicity and Early Warning Signals for Market Turbulence
sources.authors: Torben G. Andersen; Oleg Bondarenko
sources.supports: A trade-classification benchmark is required before interpreting bar-derived VPIN.
sources.limitations: Non-crypto counterevidence finds bulk-volume classification inferior to tick classification and vulnerable to volatility-induced toxicity signals.

sources.title: Fragmentation, Price Formation and Cross-Impact in Bitcoin Markets
sources.authors: Jakob Albers; Mihai Cucuringu; Sam Howison; Alexander Y. Shestopaloff
sources.supports: Synchronized trades and L2 depth explain sub-second future BTC moves; excess bid depth has an immediate positive, not contrarian, sign.
sources.limitations: The 500 ms L2 result cannot be transferred to five-minute imbalance fading without observed overshoot, normalization, queue, spread, and impact.

sources.title: Technical Analysis in Cryptocurrency Markets: Do Transaction Costs and Bubbles Matter?
sources.authors: Daniel Svogun; Walter Bazán-Palomino
sources.publication: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money
sources.supports: Moving-average and breakout rules must be compared at one-minute and daily horizons with explicit transaction costs.
sources.limitations: Generic technical-rule evidence does not validate a specific compression, VWAP, or breakout implementation.

sources.title: How to Manage a Local Order Book Correctly
sources.authors: Binance
sources.supports: Executable BBO/depth research requires a REST snapshot, ordered WebSocket updates, sequence validation, and rebuild on gaps.
sources.limitations: One-minute OHLCV cannot reconstruct historical depth imbalance, queue position, or contemporaneous executable spread.

sources.title: Crypto Carry
sources.authors: Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf; Karamfil Todorov
sources.supports: Positive cash-and-carry is a paired long-spot/short-futures position, and unusually high carry predicts elevated subsequent spot-crash risk.
sources.limitations: The paired trade's documented loss channels are interim basis widening, short-futures variation margin/liquidation under separate collateral, financing, and intermediary failure. No inspected LuminaQuant strategy or execution contract models all of them.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures
sources.authors: Songrun He; Asaf Manela; Omri Ross; Victor von Wachter
sources.supports: Perpetual funding arbitrage is random-maturity and spot-hedged; entry/exit must exceed two-leg cost bounds.
sources.limitations: Preprint/working-paper evidence; it does not support naked funding momentum.

sources.title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.authors: Igor Makarov; Antoinette Schoar
sources.supports: Cross-venue deviations coexist with segmentation, capital controls, trapped fiat, and limits to arbitrage.
sources.limitations: Close-price spread backtests without inventory, transfer latency, balances, withdrawal state, and venue default risk are not executable evidence.

sources.title: USDⓈ-M Futures Funding Rate History API
sources.authors: Binance
sources.supports: The official historical endpoint defines symbol, fundingRate, fundingTime, and markPrice fields needed to reconstruct timestamped funding observations.
sources.limitations: An API field contract is not a payment-direction specification, execution model, or historical profitability result; funding intervals and economics require point-in-time contract metadata.

sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio
sources.authors: David H. Bailey; Marcos López de Prado
sources.supports: Sharpe evidence must be deflated for selection bias, non-normality, trial count, and cross-trial Sharpe dispersion.
sources.limitations: A per-candidate num_trials=1 calculation or survivor-only trial ledger is not the published protocol.

sources.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
sources.authors: David H. Bailey; Jonathan Borwein; Marcos López de Prado; Qiji Zhu
sources.supports: CSCV/PBO evaluates a family selection procedure using the full candidate-by-time matrix.
sources.limitations: Single-series train-positive/test-negative fold frequency is not CSCV/PBO.

sources.title: A Test for Superior Predictive Ability
sources.authors: Peter R. Hansen
sources.supports: SPA tests the maximum studentized benchmark-relative performance across all alternatives with dependence-preserving bootstrap.
sources.limitations: A one-series circular block-bootstrap mean test is not Hansen SPA.

sources.title: The Statistics of Sharpe Ratios
sources.authors: Andrew W. Lo
sources.supports: Serial correlation invalidates naive square-root annualization and IID Sharpe inference, especially for overlapping high-frequency positions.
sources.limitations: It provides inference discipline, not an alpha source.

sources.title: The Properties of Equally Weighted Risk Contribution Portfolios
sources.authors: Sébastien Maillard; Thierry Roncalli; Jérôme Teïletche
sources.supports: ERC is a valid risk-budgeting challenger after alpha/evidence gates.
sources.limitations: Risk budgeting does not create alpha or rescue failed sleeves.

sources.title: Optimal Versus Naive Diversification: How Inefficient Is the 1/N Portfolio Strategy?
sources.authors: Victor DeMiguel; Lorenzo Garlappi; Raman Uppal
sources.supports: Equal weight is a required allocation benchmark; optimized portfolios do not consistently dominate out of sample.
sources.limitations: Traditional-asset allocation evidence, not crypto alpha evidence.

sources.title: Diversification Return, Portfolio Rebalancing, and the Commodity Return Puzzle
sources.authors: Scott Willenbrock
sources.supports: A constant-weight rebalanced portfolio can earn a diversification return related to constituent variance minus portfolio variance.
sources.limitations: Commodity/general portfolio arithmetic is not crypto alpha evidence; the same-basket buy-and-hold control and all rebalance costs are required.

sources.title: What Does Rebalancing Really Achieve?
sources.authors: Keith Cuthbertson; Simon Hayley; Nick Motson; Dirk Nitzsche
sources.supports: Rebalancing effects must be decomposed from diversification and asset-return effects rather than labeled mechanical alpha.
sources.limitations: Non-crypto evidence; it is a falsification/control requirement, not a forecast.

sources.title: Dacapogo authenticated upstream daily breakout source (crypto_backtest.py)
sources.authors: Hokyoung Jung
sources.publication: Dacapogo private GitHub source repository (authorized access required)
sources.supports: Direct authenticated upstream evidence for the daily top-ten previous-value-ranked 4% breakout formula reproduced by DacapogoDailySourceStrategy.
sources.limitations: The upstream repository is private and requires authorized access. It describes a transferred/reconstructed skeleton rather than the private Dacapogo algorithm; source parity is not performance or live-readiness evidence.

benchmark.title: Benchmarks and Passive Controls
benchmark.thesis: Keep cash/no-position, buy-and-hold, and simple equal-weight controls as first-class comparators; they are not alpha sleeves.

trend_momentum.title: Time-Series Trend and Momentum
trend_momentum.thesis: Prioritize slow own-return trend at 4h/1d and paper-aligned one-to-four-week crypto horizons; ablate signal from inverse-vol sizing and count every horizon.

cross_sectional.title: Cross-Sectional Momentum, Anchoring, and Factors
cross_sectional.thesis: Test point-in-time weekly return sorts and exact 52-week-nearness controls before repository-specific residualizers, young-coin fallbacks, or composite filters.

rebalancing_diversification.title: Rebalancing and Diversification Return
rebalancing_diversification.thesis: Measure only the incremental return versus a buy-and-hold portfolio initialized with the identical assets and weights; decompose asset beta, target-weight drift, turnover, and costs.

breakout.title: Breakout and Compression Continuation
breakout.thesis: Treat breakout/compression rules as repository hypotheses; validate only with next-bar fills, spread/impact, false-breakout attribution, and bounded trials.

mean_reversion_relative_value.title: Mean Reversion and Relative Value
mean_reversion_relative_value.thesis: Reversal may be liquidity compensation; prioritize stationary pairs/residuals at >=5m only when synchronized prices, spread, fees, borrow, and capacity are modeled.

microstructure_intraday.title: Microstructure and Intraday Flow
microstructure_intraday.thesis: Order-flow and lead-lag features are valid hypotheses, but OHLCV-only close execution is insufficient; require point-in-time trades/BBO/depth, latency, queue, impact, and capacity.

event_alpha.title: Event and Shock Alpha
event_alpha.thesis: Shock, opening-range, and liquidation events require timestamp-causal event data and conservative next-observation execution; bar-derived events remain hypotheses.

derivatives_carry.title: Derivatives Signals Labeled Carry
derivatives_carry.thesis: Existing single-leg funding/basis classes are directional derivatives signals, not cash-and-carry. Do not infer carry returns from their names.

derivatives_directional_crowding.title: Directional Funding, Crowding, and Liquidation Signals
derivatives_directional_crowding.thesis: Evaluate funding/OI/liquidation features only as directional crowding or crash-risk hypotheses with exact event timing; they do not implement delta-neutral carry.

volatility_risk_overlay.title: Volatility and Crash-Risk Overlays
volatility_risk_overlay.thesis: Keep scaled and unscaled variants separate, use lagged own-sleeve volatility, count overlay choices as trials, and benchmark against no scaling.

ensemble_regime_router.title: Ensembles and Regime Routers
ensemble_regime_router.thesis: Only preregistered, causally available composites with jointly netted trades may combine weak forecasts; every recipe and router is another trial.

seasonality.title: Seasonality and Calendar Effects
seasonality.thesis: Calendar rules require timezone, venue-session, holiday, and multiple-calendar correction; preserve cash when the effect is absent.

intermarket.title: Intermarket and Cross-Asset Signals
intermarket.thesis: Require synchronized point-in-time tradable clocks and asset-specific calendars/costs; never forward-fill a closed market into apparent predictability.

formulaic_alpha.title: Formulaic and Alpha-Zoo Signals
formulaic_alpha.thesis: Treat the full formula search as one family-wide multiple-testing experiment with a frozen ledger and complete candidate-by-time matrix.

unresolved.title: Unresolved or Miscellaneous Signals
unresolved.thesis: No economic label is inferred from performance. Resolve causal inputs, horizon, execution, and family before promotion.

recommended_experiments.change: Compare fixed wall-clock 1/2/3-week own-return signs with one-week decisions, long-only and long-short separately; freeze all extra gates, then ablate them one at a time.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Realistic net costs, purged validation, family-wide DSR/SPA/CSCV, then one locked report-only OOS.

recommended_experiments.change: Use 1/2/3/4-week return ranks, weekly rebalance, raw returns, zero absolute threshold, and fixed 30% tails; report each leg and point-in-time universe.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: No selection on locked OOS; include borrow/funding/liquidation and turnover costs.

recommended_experiments.change: Compare exact 52-week/full-history/weekly/10% tails against existing relaxed-history and 25% variants with weighting held fixed.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Rank IC and net spread must survive delisted/young-coin PIT universe and family-wide multiplicity.

recommended_experiments.change: Use synchronized >=5m prices, fold-local hedge/stationarity estimates, next-bar execution, explicit two-leg spread/fee/borrow, and a no-trade band.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Reject nonstationary folds, asynchronous clocks, unavailable borrow, or negative conservative-cost edge.

recommended_experiments.change: Compare unscaled, lagged own-sleeve inverse-vol, and current wrapper as three separately counted candidates with identical direction signals.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Net utility/tail improvement on purged validation; locked OOS remains report-only.

recommended_experiments.change: Replay the identical initial assets and target weights as buy-and-hold, equal-weight rebalanced, and diversity-weighted rebalanced arms; attribute market/constituent return, excess growth, turnover, and cost separately.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Only incremental net return versus the same-basket buy-and-hold control counts; current total-return rank is diagnostic and cannot establish a rebalancing premium.

recommended_experiments.change: Do not add a production strategy yet. First prove same-venue BTC/ETH spot and perp streams, actual funding events, paired fills, residual-delta invariant, separate collateral, fees, basis PnL, and financing. Then test zero-leverage long spot/short perp only.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: No negative-funding reverse carry without historical spot borrow; no profit claim without both-leg accounting and margin stress.

recommended_experiments.change: Predeclare large 1m/5m displacement events and 1/5/60/120-minute exits; compare VWAP-only, calm BVC-VPIN gate, high-toxicity gate, and time/volatility/volume-matched placebos.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Only next-observation net edge after actual fee, spread, impact, funding, latency, adverse-selection buffer, and family-wide multiplicity can pass.

recommended_experiments.change: Use BTC t-1 only, synchronized closes, reject stale bars, rank laggards by past-only trade count/dollar volume, and compare liquid-major controls against low-liquidity alts.
recommended_experiments.promotion_gate: Reject unless effect strength declines monotonically with liquidity and exceeds venue-specific all-in cost at a capacity-constrained size.

hard_rejections: Online or paper Sharpe/return headlines are not LuminaQuant returns.
Do not create another trend, near-high, pairs, or volatility class before existing classes pass paper-aligned ablations.
Do not call a single-leg funding, OI, basis, or liquidation strategy carry/arbitrage.
Do not promote minute lead-lag, order-flow, reversal, or VPIN from OHLCV close fills without BBO/tick economics.
Do not select, weight, filter, or fall back using locked OOS metrics.
Do not use approximate single-series PBO or SPA-like p-values as genuine family-wide CSCV/PBO or Hansen SPA.
Do not optimize an allocator on non-co-dated returns or allow renormalization to breach weight caps.
